key_insight: This paper introduces FlatSounds, a benchmark that tests whether video-to-audio models understand real physical causality, not just whether they generate realistic-sounding audio. It reveals how well models respond to controlled changes in a single physical factor.
problem_solved: Current V2A evaluations focus mostly on perceptual realism and do not check if generated audio is physically correct when the video changes in a controlled way. This paper addresses the gap by benchmarking physical reasoning under counterfactual and single-video intervention settings.
method: Create controlled counterfactual video pairs where only one physical factor changes at a time.
Test whether V2A models produce audio that changes consistently with the manipulated factor.
Use single-video pattern tests to probe physical cues without needing paired comparisons.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more rigorous way to evaluate V2A models beyond surface-level realism. It can help identify models that sound plausible but fail to capture true physical dynamics, guiding better model design and evaluation.
